personalIntent.goal: Investigate a nearby tree for usable materials without compromising my food reserve.
personalIntent.reason: Root crushing requires stone and bark that I do not own. Birch 6 also reports not finding them; nearby trees currently show branches, not confirmed bark supplies.
personalIntent.progress: Health is 100, satiety 73.3 and energy 31.8. I carry three roots and have mastered root preparation, but have not tested it.
personalIntent.next: Approach the nearby tree and observe it before deciding whether material collection needs a new capability.
personalIntent.pause: Reconsider after observation, navigation failure, injury or a local hazard.

shown.question: Can available roots be practically prepared using real reusable implements?
evidence: A root eaten at tick 7 provided 14 nutrition.
At tick 23 I carry three roots but no stone or bark.
The mastered preparation contract requires actual stone and bark and preserves nutrition and toxicity.
Birch 6 reported at tick 20 that they had not located stone or bark.
shown.uncertainty: Whether the nearby tree can supply bark is unknown; no preparation benefit has been demonstrated.
shown.goal: Perform one feasible preparation trial while retaining a safe food reserve.
shown.missing: Actual stone and bark and a reachable worksite.
shown.next: Observe the nearby tree for evidence about accessible materials.
shown.benefit: Raw roots provide a known food reserve; preparation remains untested.

shown.subject: Preservation materials
shown.text: I have not located stone or bark. I learned root air drying: its tray needs two stone and one bark, and drying is slow and weather-dependent. I will inspect a nearby tree and explore a short distance east for materials; no preservation result yet.

shown: Tree branch stock does not establish an accessible bark supply.
Known roots provide 14 nutrition and have zero known toxicity.
